short: Spreading an asset's cost across the years it is used.
metaDescription: Depreciation spreads the cost of a fixed asset across the years it is expected to be useful, instead of charging the whole amount in the year of purchase.
definition: Depreciation spreads the cost of a fixed asset across the years it is expected to be useful, instead of charging the whole amount in the year of purchase. It is a non-cash expense that reduces both profit and the asset's book value.
bodyHtml:
Why Depreciation matters

Without depreciation, buying an oven makes one month look terrible and every following month look artificially good. It is also a genuine cost: equipment wears out and must eventually be replaced.

Depreciation formula

Straight-line depreciation = (Cost − Salvage value) ÷ Useful life in years

Written-down value instead applies a fixed percentage to the reducing balance.

How Depreciation works in practice

Pick a method and useful life per asset class and apply it consistently. Note that accounting depreciation and the rates permitted for tax often differ, so two schedules are normal.

Worked example

A ₹3,00,000 oven with a ₹30,000 salvage value over 6 years depreciates at ₹45,000 a year.

faq.question: Is depreciation a cash expense?
faq.answer: No cash moves, but the cost is real — the asset is being consumed and will need replacing.

faq.question: Which method should I use?
faq.answer: Straight line is simplest and suits assets used evenly; written-down value front-loads the charge and often matches tax treatment.
